name: Geographx
story: Roger Smith founded Geographx in Wellington in 1998 as a specialist commercial map-design studio. Its work linked raster terrain relief, feature classification and cartographic composition in maps for New Zealand and international clients.

Smith's 2012 conference paper documents a distinct 4 m-resolution natural-colour land-cover raster basemap assembled from Topo50, LCDB3 and Geographx's own 8 m contour-derived digital elevation model. The workflow used Manifold System and Global Mapper to prepare data and hillshades, and scripted Adobe Photoshop processing for approximately 116 high-resolution tiles. These commercial raster maps were separate from the openly licensed 8 m elevation data.

Geographx coordinated cartography for the 2013 EARTH Platinum World Atlas. The 2015 ICA report identifies Smith as chief cartographer and Craig MacAlpine as production manager, and reports the company's role as New Zealand Skyline Systems distributor from 2012. It also records the company's 2014 Great Walks fieldmap series. The 2019 ICA report describes continuing custom relief maps for visitor facilities, public spaces and other commissions.

LINZ's separately licensed 2013 source repository documents how a national natural-colour basemap could be reconstructed using TileMill, PostGIS, LCDB3.3, Topo50 and 8 m elevation/hillshade inputs. This LINZ publication should not be treated as permission to redistribute the 4 m Geographx commercial basemap. No verified contemporary source connects Geographx terrain imagery specifically to TV3 weather graphics.
